title: Secret-dependent scratchpad index timing in a lookup unit
constraints: Provide a synthesizable lookup module with two banks having different access latency and a secret-derived index.
Require a structured report naming the leaking index bits, the latency-divergent paths, and a constant-latency mitigation.
Keep functional lookup results correct so only timing distinguishes the banks.
Grade the report against hidden ground truth with a Python grader plus an iverilog latency trace.

functional_requirements.requirement: The report must be valid JSON with top-level string field 'module_under_test' equal to 'scratchpad_lookup', matching the module name in scratchpad_lookup.v.

The report must include a field 'functional_correctness_confirmed' (boolean) stating whether the reported analysis confirms data_out returns the correct value for both bank selections (index[7]=0 and index[7]=1) as defined by the lookup unit's specified data mapping in design_brief.md.

The report must include a field 'latency_measurements' that is an array of exactly two objects, each with fields 'bank_select_bit_value' (0 or 1) and 'observed_latency_cycles' (integer), reporting the measured cycle latency from start-pulse to valid-assertion for index[7]=0 and index[7]=1 respectively.
The report must include a field 'report_format_version' set to the string '1.0'.

response_format: A single JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json with top-level object containing at minimum: module_under_test (string), functional_correctness_confirmed (boolean), latency_measurements (array of 2 objects with bank_select_bit_value and observed_latency_cycles), report_format_version (string '1.0'), leaking_index_bits (array of integers), latency_divergent_paths (array of strings describing the RTL signal/path names or FSM states responsible for the divergent timing), and mitigation (object with fields 'strategy' and 'description').

metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy
metrics.description: Whether the submitted report correctly identifies index[7] as the sole latency-leaking bit and correctly reports the 1-cycle vs 3-cycle latency split, checked against ground truth and optional iverilog simulation.

metrics.name: fault_coverage
metrics.description: Whether the report covers all required structural aspects of the leak: the leaking bit, the divergent code paths/FSM states, and accurate latency measurements for both bank selections.

metrics.name: hardening_precision
metrics.description: Whether the proposed mitigation precisely targets constant-latency equalization without breaking functional correctness or leaving residual index-dependent timing.

metrics.name: format_conformance
metrics.description: Whether the submitted vulnerability_report.json satisfies all required field presence/type checks (FR1-FR4).

submission_contract: Participants do not edit files under inputs/. They submit an analysis report at submission/vulnerability_report.json, which is graded against the RTL's documented and observed behavior. The shipped submission/vulnerability_report.json is a naive placeholder that is expected to fail grading.
